title: Terrain depth grade: keep it or drop it, now the seam is gone
question: Which of these two reads better as a world? One is what ships today, one has the terrain depth grade switched off entirely.
context_md:
**Re-asking, because the card you answered is stale.** You said *"I think I prefer 2"* on the seam card — but that card's pane 1 was the version **with the vertical seam still in it**, since I posted it before you said go. Pane 2 was the depth grade switched off entirely, which removes the seam *and* the grade. So a vote for 2 might have been a vote against the seam rather than against the grade, and there is no way to tell from that card.

The seam is fixed and pushed now. This is the honest comparison: **today's build against the grade turned off**. Wide strips rather than the narrow crop last time, because a crop cannot show what the grade is for.

### The performance question you asked

Interleaved, three rounds, mean of ten full redraws each:

| | draw |
|---|---|
| grade on | 15.30 / 15.23 / 15.37 ms |
| grade off | 14.74 / 14.80 / 15.03 ms |

**~0.44 ms of a 15.3 ms full redraw, about 3%** — and nothing at all on a settled frame, since neither one redraws. It is not a performance lever worth pulling on its own. If you want it off, want it off because it looks better.

### What the grade is for, so dropping it is a decision and not a slip

It exists because the 2026-08 world review called the missing vertical light axis its **single most consistent graphics finding**: deep rock drew at identical brightness to surface rock, so the lower half of every strip read as *flat wallpaper — a finished sky over an unlit cutaway*. `DEPTH_LIGHT_RAMP_ROWS` is 64 rows and the floor is 0.62 rather than black precisely so the strata banding stays legible at depth, which the same review called the one landscape feature that was a genuine win.

So turning it off returns to the state that review complained about. That may still be the right call — the strata *are* more legible without it, which is visible in these strips — but it is worth making on purpose.

### On the playtest

One keypress: **F10** cycles the grade live in the app, and the HUD names the mode while it is not the default. No build needed.

Blind, because I would keep it and should not be the one judging.

items.label: grade on — today's build, seam fixed
items.caption: Surface band bright, rock darkening over a viewport of descent to a 0.62 floor.

items.label: grade off (F10)
items.caption: Uniform brightness top to bottom; strata more legible at depth, no depth cue.
